title: Optimizely Web Experimentation signup-flow flaw abused to inject skimmer, wallet swapper and iOS exploit kits into 178 organizations' scripts (OPTIMJACK)
why: Optimizely confirmed an attacker exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to write malicious JavaScript into customer projects; Report URI (Scott Helme) found 188 infected snippets for 178 organizations on Nov 16 (Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, HSBC and others), confirmed by BleepingComputer and The Hacker News. It is a hosted-service flaw with no CVE, so it cannot be in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance for it. Nov 17: Optimizely's status notice confirms an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and says it is fixed. Hudson Rock and researcher Kirk of Ohey traced the same loader in Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly responses as early as Nov 13 (Help Net Security, infostealers.com). Still no CVE, and nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Nov 18: Optimizely's statement to Gizmodo/ABC confirms the signup-flow exploit and the fix; Zoom disabled Optimizely in production. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Nov 18: Zimperium and Censys (OTX) report iOS Coruna/DarkSword kits delivered via the poisoned scripts on 21+ major sites; still no CVE, not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Nov 19: Socket, SecurityScorecard and ReversingLabs published analyses (via OTX) confirming the 188 snippets / 178 organizations count; still no CVE and nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV. Nov 20: Zscaler ThreatLabz report (via OTX) confirms the Nov 16 signup-flow exploitation and payload delivery through Optimizely's CDN snippets.
action: If you use Optimizely Web, review every project's Project JavaScript and experiment custom code for script you did not write (Report URI's checklist), rotate Optimizely users/API tokens, treat card data and non-HttpOnly cookies from Nov 16 pages as exposed, and push iOS/iPadOS to 18.7.3+ or 26.3+.
product: Optimizely Web Experimentation (hosted snippet / Project JavaScript); downstream iOS/iPadOS older than 18.7.3 / 26.3 targeted by the delivered kits

title: Java4Shell: OpenJDK AVX-512 Base64 decoder heap overflow enabling pre-auth RCE in Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak and others
why: Calif disclosed Java4Shell on Nov 17 and published a memory-corruption reproducer. It says it got pre-auth RCE on default Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, but has not released those exploits. Oracle fixed it in the Nov 17 CSPU (CVSS 3.1 8.1; Calif rates it CVSS 4.0 9.2), and Horizon3, Rapid7, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and oss-security cover it. Reports say the Microsoft Build of OpenJDK is affected, but as of Nov 18 Microsoft had not published a fixed build and MSRC has no advisory. It is not in CISA KEV. watchTowr and Upwind report no exploitation in the wild yet. Nov 17-18: CISA alert urges immediate patching (not a KEV listing); Fortinet FG-IR-26-278 and Cisco advisories published; OX/SecurityWeek: still no public RCE exploit or ITW; still not in KEV, no MSRC advisory. Nov 18 19Z: Cloudflare shipped WAF protection and the Swiss NCSC issued a warning; still no exploitation in the wild reported and not in CISA KEV (not among today's four KEV additions). Nov 19: Tenable reports GreyNoise exploitation attempts (none confirmed successful) and a working VulnCheck exploit for its customers; still not in CISA KEV (no KEV additions since Nov 18), no MSRC advisory. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Nov 19 23Z: Palo Alto Networks published a portfolio status advisory for CVE-2026-114938. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Update Java runtimes to the Nov 17 fixed builds (Oracle/Amazon out; for Temurin, Zulu, Microsoft and Red Hat, watch for their builds). Until then, start the JVMs behind Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, or -XX:UseAVX=2.
product: OpenJDK-based Java runtimes 17.0.6 and later (Java 17, 21, 25, 27; Oracle Java 8 Performance Pack) on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI

title: VMware vCenter VMware Directory Service auth bypass (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) exploited as a zero-day since September by China-nexus Armory Castle
why: Broadcom fixed CVE-2026-123890 in VMSA-2026-0009 on Nov 19, and on the same day Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group said the China-nexus espionage group Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) has exploited it as a zero-day since early September 2026, using a tool called Bonesaw to gain vCenter admin, create SSO admin accounts, steal cryptographic material and plant backdoors (Rapid7, The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, SecurityOnline, Cyber Kendra). Broadcom's advisory does not mention exploitation. As of Nov 20 it is not in CISA KEV (Rescana, Cyber Kendra; no KEV additions since Nov 18), and there is no Microsoft signal. Nov 20: GTIG's full report says BONESAW was run in early September against a vCenter already patched for CVE-2026-59309 (that fix does not block it), the intrusion began via BeyondTrust CVE-2026-102764, and Computing.net reports no public patch for end-of-support vCenter 7.0. Rechecked Nov 20 17Z: still not in CISA KEV (last additions Nov 18).
action: Patch vCenter to 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 U3m or 5.2.5 now, restrict vCenter access to admin networks, and hunt for unexpected SSO administrator accounts and new files or services on vCenter appliances since September.
product: VMware vCenter 9.1.x before 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.x before 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 before 8.0 U3m, 5.x before 5.2.5

title: Cisco Expressway clustered database service: unauthenticated root RCE via hard-coded cluster cookie, exploited in the wild after public PoC
why: F6 reported on Nov 19 that attackers used the public PoC (GitHub, Nov 5) to root four clustered Expressway gateways at a Russian organization and move laterally (THN, SecurityWeek, Security Affairs, Ostorlab). Ostorlab states it is not in CISA KEV as of Nov 20, and our KEV recheck (last additions Nov 18) agrees. Not a Microsoft product; nothing from Microsoft/Defender on it.
action: Upgrade every node of Expressway clusters to X15.5.20; until then restrict TCP 4371/4372 to cluster peers and check System > Status for unexpected cluster peers.
product: Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E (clustered) X15.5.3 and earlier, including X14 and earlier

title: Apache Roller XML-RPC pre-auth Java deserialization RCE (4.0.0-6.1.4), Apache says actively exploited
why: Apache's Nov 17 advisory for CVE-2026-129448 says the flaw 'is being actively exploited'. It widens the September CVE-2026-82384 (6.1.5 only) back to 4.0.0, so scanners keyed on the old record miss older installs. Public PoCs for 82384 exist on GitHub and Sploitus. SecurityOnline reports it is not in CISA KEV, and CISA's last KEV additions were on Nov 13. Microsoft has published nothing on it. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Nov 18: The Hacker News reports the ASF confirmation of active exploitation; still not in CISA KEV as of today's additions. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Roller to 6.1.6 or later. Until then, set enabledForExtensions=false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart, then check that host for unexpected JVM child processes.
product: Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.5 (fixed in 6.1.6)

title: NGINX2Root: unauthenticated RCE in nginx HTTP/2 (CVE-2026-123007) plus four more nginx worker RCEs; Rapid7 PoC public, kernel SCTP chain to root unpatched
why: On Nov 18, F5 (K000163926), Rapid7, Wiz and Xint disclosed CVE-2026-123007, an HTTP/2 flow-control integer underflow (CVSS 4.0 9.2) that gives unauthenticated code execution as the nginx worker. It affects every nginx release from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8 with HTTP/2 enabled, and Wiz showed it working on a server that only serves static files. Rapid7 published a proof of concept on GitHub. Xint says it has working exploits for all five nginx CVEs, and that a separate, still-unpatched Linux SCTP flaw takes the worker to host root, including out of a Docker container. CIRCL (TR-105), LWN and Precursor Security also cover it. Precursor and Upwind report no exploitation in the wild yet, and none of the CVEs is in CISA KEV. Nov 18 19Z: The Hacker News, watchTowr, OX Security, SecurityOnline and Cyber Kendra now cover it (Hacker News front page, 588 points). All still say no exploitation in the wild, and it is still not in CISA KEV (today's KEV additions were LiteLLM, Apache Axis, Synology and REDCap). Nov 19: Wiz independently reproduced the bugs; set also covers CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-113425; Qualys says working exploit code is public; oss-security notes the SCTP kernel LPE in the root chain is still unpatched. No ITW, not in KEV. Nov 19 PM: BleepingComputer and LWN covered NGINX2Root, and a Hacker News post says GitLab 19.6.0 still ships an affected nginx. Still no reported exploitation in the wild. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Nov 19: Tenable and StepSecurity still report no exploitation in the wild; Debian fixed trixie (DSA-6642-1) but bookworm is still vulnerable (oss-security). Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade nginx to 1.30.7 or 1.31.9 (NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1/37.3.0.1), or your distro's fixed package, and restart it, because a reload does not load the new binary. Rebuild nginx container images on explicit 1.31.9/1.30.7 tags. Until then, turn off HTTP/2 on internet-facing listeners, and block the sctp kernel module where it isn't needed.
product: nginx Open Source 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 with HTTP/2 enabled (fixed 1.30.7 stable, 1.31.9 mainline); NGINX Plus 37.x before 37.0.8.1/37.3.0.1 and R34-R36 (no fix for R34-R36)

title: Oracle Database: pre-auth RCE chain (Oracle Text CVE-2026-114819 + ORDS GraphQL CVE-2026-91609) with public PoC from Depthfirst
why: Depthfirst researcher Zheng Yu published proof-of-concept exploits on Nov 18, and The Hacker News reported them on Nov 19. One is a chain that reaches Oracle Database engine code and runs commands with no login, through an exposed ORDS GraphQL endpoint. Oracle patched the parts in its Nov 17 CSPU (CVE-2026-114819, CVSS 9.9) and Oct 20 CPU (CVE-2026-91609), but rates neither as exploitable without a login. No attacks have been seen. Neither CVE is in CISA KEV, and there is nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Apply Oracle's Oct 2026 CPU (ORDS) and Nov 17 CSPU (Oracle Text) now, and take ORDS/GraphQL endpoints off the internet until both are in place.
product: Oracle Database (Oracle Text) 19.3-19.32, 21.3-21.24, 23.4.0-23.26.3 with Oracle REST Data Services 24.2.0-26.2.1 exposed

title: WP Duplicate (LocalSync) WordPress plugin <=1.1.11: unauthenticated file upload to RCE, exploited, no patch
why: WPScan, the CNA, says the flaw is being actively exploited in the wild. A public exploit (Duplicate2Shell) was indexed on Sploitus and Vulners on Nov 15, and SecurityOnline reports that no patch exists. Microsoft has no advisory, and the flaw is not in CISA KEV, whose last additions were on Nov 13. WPScan has not published attack volumes or IOCs. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Nov 19: NVD published CVE-2026-14492 (CVSS 9.8) for WP Duplicate through 1.1.11: RCE via save_single_batch_file through a type-juggling auth bypass plus path traversal. It may be the same flaw under a second CVE (unconfirmed). Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Deactivate and delete WP Duplicate from every WordPress site. Then look in wp-content/uploads and the plugin directories for PHP files you did not put there, and rotate admin credentials if you find any.
product: WP Duplicate WordPress plugin through 1.1.11 (no fixed release)

title: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI releases 1.26.1/1.26.2 hijacked with Azure/GitHub Actions credential stealer
why: On Nov 17 two malicious releases of Microsoft's official agent-framework package (about 192k downloads a month) were uploaded outside its release pipeline. Each installs a .pth hook that steals Azure, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions and CI credentials on every Python start. Socket, OX Security, SafeDep, Aikido, Wiz and others reported it (The Hacker News, OTX). PyPI quarantined both versions. I found no MSRC advisory, Microsoft statement or Defender guidance. A public GitHub issue says it is unconfirmed whether the upload credential has been revoked. As a supply-chain incident with no CVE, it cannot be in CISA KEV. Nov 18: SecurityWeek says an Agent Framework maintainer acknowledged it in a GitHub discussion (versions removed, investigation under way); still no MSRC advisory or Defender guidance. Nov 18 19Z: BleepingComputer says Microsoft had not answered its questions by publication time; still no MSRC advisory or Defender guidance. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Nov 19: Elastic Security Labs (caught it six minutes after publication) and JFrog published analyses of the .pth credential stealer in 1.26.1/1.26.2 (via OTX). Still no Microsoft advisory found. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Search lockfiles, pip/uv caches, CI caches and internal mirrors for agent-framework 1.26.1/1.26.2. Pin 1.26.0, rebuild affected hosts from clean images, and rotate every Azure, GitHub and cloud credential reachable from them, including OIDC trust for GitHub Actions jobs that ran with id-token: write.
product: agent-framework (PyPI) 1.26.1 and 1.26.2

title: FastUnlock: Windows 11 Narrator lock-screen bypass 0-day defeats BitLocker on fully patched 26H2 (public PoC)
why: On Nov 19 the researcher behind the MSNightmare account published FastUnlock on GitHub, a Windows Narrator lock-screen bypass he says gives code execution as the lock-screen account 'WsiAccount' and bypasses BitLocker on Windows 11 26H2 with the November patch. He suggests chaining it with SignDrop to elevate privileges. It spread via X, Hacker News and GitHub trending. There is no CVE, no MSRC advisory and no Microsoft statement yet. Not independently confirmed. Nov 20: The Hacker News, Cyber Press and Cryptika covered it; Cryptika says no Microsoft fix was identified as of Nov 20, and the November BitLocker fixes (CVE-2026-97015, CVE-2026-119832) are unrelated. Still no CVE or MSRC advisory.
action: For high-risk laptops, require a BitLocker pre-boot PIN (TPM+PIN) and watch MSRC for a fix. If your accessibility policy allows it, consider blocking Narrator at the lock screen.
product: Windows 11 26H2 with the November 2026 update (researcher's claim)

title: Drupal core installer flaw lets anonymous attackers reinstall the site: takeover or RCE (SA-CORE-2026-017)
why: Drupal's security team published SA-CORE-2026-017 (Critical 18/25, CVE-2026-132165) on Nov 18 and warned that exploits may appear within hours or days; BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and The DropTimes covered it Nov 19. No attacks reported yet, and it is not in CISA KEV. Microsoft has nothing on it. Nov 19-20: Drupal's risk vector marks the exploit as E:Proof (proof of concept exists), and Horizon3 published an analysis; THN and Cyber Kendra covered it. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. No in-the-wild reports yet; not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13, and block web access to /core/install.php and make settings.php read-only for the web server.

title: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 hosts exploited to deploy XMRig at 13 organizations (likely known unauthenticated WebCam Server RCE)
why: Huntress SOC saw attackers abuse internet-exposed GeoVision GV-VMS at 13 organizations (most activity Nov 8-10): commands spawned by GeoStartupAgentService.exe as SYSTEM, a BYOVD driver and IFEO hijacks to disable Microsoft Defender, then a DHT/PKARR Go loader and XMRig. Huntress told Help Net Security (Nov 16) that the sampled hosts ran GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 and that one of three unauthenticated RCEs in GeoVision's April 2026 advisory is the most likely entry point, but the exact CVE is not confirmed. No CVE for this activity is in CISA KEV and there is no Microsoft guidance; the campaign actively tries to switch Defender off. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade GV-VMS to V17.4.8.58 or later, take GeoVision management interfaces off the internet (VPN/IP allowlist), and hunt for cmd/PowerShell children of GeoStartupAgentService.exe and IFEO Debugger keys on Defender processes.
product: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 (older than fixed V17.4.8.58)

title: Danfoss refrigeration controllers: CVEs assigned for default-credential access (AK-SC 355/AK-SM 800, used in the supermarket sabotage wave) and an unauthenticated CGI overflow (AK-SM 8xxA)
why: Danfoss advisory DSA-2026-12-01 (published Nov 20) assigns CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9) to the factory default credentials on legacy AK-SC 355/AK-SM 800 controllers and CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3) to an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA. Reporting on the European refrigeration-sabotage wave (decryptiondigest, SOCRadar) names default credentials on internet-exposed AK-SM 800A/8xxA as an entry point. Neither new CVE is in CISA KEV. Whether 129713 is one of the six unpatched AK-SM800A flaws disclosed Nov 11 is not confirmed.
action: Take AK-SC/AK-SM controllers off the internet (VPN only), change the default Supervisor credentials now, and follow DSA-2026-12-01 for AK-SM 8xxA firmware.
product: Danfoss legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series (all versions); AK-SM 8xxA Series

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-116331: low-privilege login role to OS code execution via type confusion (public Depthfirst PoC)
why: Depthfirst published a working exploit on Nov 18 (reported by The Hacker News, Nov 19). In it, a plain login role that uses only its default TEMPORARY privilege runs code as the database OS user. PostgreSQL fixed it on Nov 12. No exploitation in the wild has been reported, it is not in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has published no guidance (Azure Database for PostgreSQL status unknown). Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade PostgreSQL to 18.7/17.12/16.16/15.20/14.25, and revoke TEMPORARY from roles that do not need it.

title: ClickHouse integer-overflow write in binary row format reached by low-privilege user (public Depthfirst PoC, no CVE, no confirmed fix)
why: Depthfirst reproduced a shell on ClickHouse 26.7.5.10 from a user who only sets format_binary_max_string_size=0. The PoC was published Nov 18 (The Hacker News, Nov 19). It has no CVE and no confirmed fixed version, so it cannot be in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has published nothing. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Restrict who can change settings on ClickHouse (use a readonly or settings-constraint profile that locks format_binary_max_string_size), and ask ClickHouse for a fixed build.
product: ClickHouse (26.7.5.10 tested)

title: N-able Mail Assure / SpamExperts Hosted Cloud server breached; management portal and APIs disabled in 3 regions
why: On Nov 18 N-able confirmed that unknown attackers reached one server in its Mail Assure/SpamExperts Hosted Cloud and disabled management interfaces and APIs across the Americas, EMEA and APAC (The Hacker News, Cyber Security News, CyberPress, GBHackers). N-able says it found no evidence of customer data or mailbox access, and the investigation is ongoing. The entry point is not disclosed, so there is no CVE or KEV entry, and Microsoft has nothing on it. N-able says it is unrelated to the N-central incident. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV. Nov 20: N-able says the attackers who breached one of its servers caused a worldwide outage of Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud (BleepingComputer).
action: If you or your MSP use Mail Assure/SpamExperts, confirm you received N-able's guidance, then review quarantine-release and outbound-relay activity and rotate the portal and API credentials once access is restored.
product: Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud

title: SAPBleed / ICM2SHELL: pre-auth WebSocket heap overflow in SAP ICM, Web Dispatcher and HANA XS (memory leak of SSO tickets and TLS keys, RCE)
why: nullFaktor published full technical details and a demo video on Full Disclosure on Nov 17. Without credentials, it read arbitrary ICM memory, pulled the server's TLS private key and a valid MYSAPSSO2 SSO ticket, and demonstrated RCE. Onapsis gave SAP a working exploit. SAP patched it on Nov 10 (CVSS 10.0). No exploit code is public and no exploitation has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has no advisory or Defender coverage for it. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Apply SAP Security Notes 3778530 (ICM kernel/dw.sar) and 3778556 (Web Dispatcher and HANA XS). Until patched, block WebSocket upgrades at the Web Dispatcher. After patching, rotate the TLS keys and invalidate SSO tickets on exposed systems.
product: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP ICM, SAP Web Dispatcher, SAP HANA XS internal Web Dispatcher (see SAP Notes 3778530, 3778556)

title: MySQL Server/Cluster optimizer flaw CVE-2026-101786: temp-table-only account to RCE (public Depthfirst PoC)
why: Depthfirst published a PoC on Nov 18 showing code execution on MySQL 26.7.0 from an account that can only create temporary tables. Oracle's Oct 20 advisory rates the flaw as needing high privileges. No exploitation has been seen, it is not in CISA KEV, and there is nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Update MySQL 26.7.x to the October 2026 fixed release, and remove CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES from accounts that do not need it.
product: MySQL Server and Cluster 26.7.0 to 26.7.1

title: Ruby2Shell (CVE-2026-132825): one-byte heap overflow in Ruby case conversion, pre-auth RCE on stock Rails and classic Sinatra
why: Ruby2Shell (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5) now has CVE-2026-132825 (Aikido, Astra; MITRE CVSS 7.4). Ruby maintainers know of private PoCs that achieve RCE in some scenarios, and Veria Labs plans a public PoC about a week after the Nov 19 disclosure. A Hacker News post says GitLab 19.6.0 still ships an affected Ruby. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV, and nothing from Microsoft. Nov 19: MITRE assigned CVE-2026-132825 (oss-security). Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Ruby to 3.3.14, 3.4.13 or 4.0.10 and restart app processes. Check the Ruby bundled inside GitLab and other appliances or containers, and patch internet-facing Rails apps before the public PoC lands.
product: CRuby 2.4.0 through 3.3.13, 3.4.0-3.4.12, 4.0.0-4.0.9 (also bundled runtimes in GitLab and other self-hosted apps)

title: F5 BIG-IP out-of-band hotfixes: five critical unauthenticated TMM stack overflows (APM, iRules) that may allow RCE
why: F5's Nov 18 out-of-band notification (K000164058/K000164239) fixes critical stack overflows that let a remote unauthenticated attacker crash TMM and may allow code execution; BleepingComputer, THN and SecurityWeek cover it. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV, nothing from Microsoft. Shadowserver sees 177,000+ exposed BIG-IP and 14,600 APM instances.
action: Check BIG-IP APM and iRule (including DNS::scrape) usage against F5's K articles and install the out-of-band hotfixes on exposed systems.
product: F5 BIG-IP (APM, iRules configurations, BIG-IP DNS DNS::scrape iRule)

title: Cyrus SASL SRP mechanism authentication bypass: A=N forces zero shared secret (CVE-2026-129483)
why: VulnCheck (CNA) published it Nov 15 with an upstream fix commit and oss-security post; CVSS 9.1/9.3, network, no privileges. No exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV. Only servers that enable the SRP SASL mechanism are exposed. A Microsoft CSAF/VEX record exists for the package, but no Microsoft product guidance. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Check whether any service offers the SRP SASL mechanism (mech_list / installed libsrp plugin) and disable or remove the SRP plugin until distro packages carry upstream commit fb3724f.
product: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 (SRP server mechanism)

title: Arize Phoenix unauthenticated applyChatTemplate format-string flaw leaks PHOENIX_SECRET, enabling admin session forgery (CVSS 10.0)
why: GitHub advisory GHSA-gfv3-m769-5xm3 and the CVE record (published Nov 16) describe an endpoint that is unauthenticated on default installs and exposes PHOENIX_SECRET, allowing admin session-token forgery. No public exploit or in-the-wild use reported; not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft coverage. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. title: Oracle Nov 2026 CSPU: unauthenticated CVSS 9.8-10.0 flaws in Access Manager, WebLogic, Platform Security for Java, BI EE, E-Business Suite
why: Oracle's Nov 17 CSPU (655 fixes) includes several flaws an unauthenticated attacker can reach over HTTP or SOAP: Access Manager auth engine 91500 and 91510 (10.0, scope change), WebLogic takeover 91456 and 91470 (9.8), Platform Security for Java 114824 (10.0), and EBS 114924 and 114925 (9.8). title: HPE Aruba AOS-10 PAPI authentication bypass (CVSS 10.0) gives unauthenticated admin access; CVE record published Nov 18
why: HPE published CVE-2026-95787 on Nov 18 (CVSS 3.1 10.0): a flaw in AOS-10's PAPI protocol lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass authentication and gain admin access. The affected ranges in the record match HPE's October bulletin HPESBNW05162, which fixed a PAPI bypass that bulletin had numbered CVE-2026-79845, a number that belonged to an unrelated CVE. So this is likely the corrected ID, but that is an inference. I found no public exploit or reports of exploitation, and it is not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Make sure every AOS-10 device runs 10.4.1.14, 10.7.2.7, 10.8.1.2 or later (the HPESBNW05162 fixed builds), and that PAPI (UDP 8211) and the management interfaces cannot be reached from the internet, guest networks or user networks.

title: PHP Nov 19 security release fixes 18 CVEs incl. critical RCEs (FPM request smuggling CVE-2026-129289, PHPAfterShell, session serializer)
why: PHP shipped 8.5.13/8.4.28/8.3.37/8.2.36 on Nov 19, fixing 18 CVEs (Aikido, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Infosecurity). The worst is CVE-2026-129289 (9.2): unauthenticated PHP-FPM request smuggling to code execution when the web server reuses backend connections. Several other session and use-after-free bugs are rated 9.2 RCE, including Depthfirst's 'PHPAfterShell' CVE-2026-126714. PHP says the critical issues need non-default or uncommon setups. No exploitation or public PoC is reported, none is in KEV, and Microsoft has nothing on them. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. Until then, disable persistent web-server-to-FPM connections and set session.upload_progress.enabled=0, and never expose FPM/LSAPI listeners to untrusted networks.
product: PHP 8.2 before 8.2.36, 8.3 before 8.3.37, 8.4 before 8.4.28, 8.5 before 8.5.13

title: Attackers used CyberPower PowerPanel Business UPS software as a SYSTEM execution channel on a domain controller to dump AD
why: In research published Nov 18, Symantec's Threat Intelligence team describes an intrusion where attackers uploaded .cmd scripts through PowerPanel Business's file-upload endpoint (TCP 3052) on a Windows domain controller. The PPB service (ppbed.exe) ran them as SYSTEM to copy the AD database and launch malware. Infosecurity Magazine also covered it. Symantec did not establish how the attackers got console access; earlier PPB advisories list hard-coded credentials and a default admin password. There is no new CVE and no KEV entry, and Microsoft has nothing on it. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Find PowerPanel Business installs, block TCP 3052 from non-admin networks, change default and admin credentials, and review the event-script folder for .cmd files you did not create.
product: PowerPanel Business (web console on TCP 3052)

title: Oracle E-Business Suite: CVE-2026-114924 auth bypass + CVE-2026-114925 REST RCE chain to unauthenticated OS command execution (12.2.3-12.2.15)
why: Horizon3 reverse engineered Oracle's November CSPU patch and published on Nov 19 that CVE-2026-114924 (authorization bypass) chains with CVE-2026-114925 (unrestricted class instantiation in REST Services) to give unauthenticated OS command execution on the EBS application tier over HTTP. Oracle reports no exploitation and no public exploit code was seen, but EBS was mass-exploited after similar disclosures earlier this year. Not in CISA KEV as of Nov 20 and no Microsoft signal.
action: Apply the November 2026 Oracle CSPU EBS patches now; until then restrict access to EBS HTTP and REST endpoints to trusted networks.
product: Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2.3-12.2.15 (Application Object Library Core; Applications Framework REST Services)

title: phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714): PHP default file session handler can be made to deserialize attacker objects, leading to RCE with a gadget chain
why: depthfirst disclosed phpAfterShell on Nov 19 with an end-to-end demonstration: interrupting a write to PHP's default file-based session storage can splice sessions so session_start() returns attacker-chosen objects, which an app gadget chain can turn into code execution (CVSS 4.0 9.2). PHP fixed it in the Nov 19 releases; The Hacker News, Cycode and Ostorlab covered it. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV (only the October PHP2Shell CVEs are), and no Microsoft signal.
action: Upgrade PHP to 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (or 8.6.0); replace EOL 8.1-and-older runtimes.
product: PHP 8.2 before 8.2.36, 8.3 before 8.3.37, 8.4 before 8.4.28, 8.5 before 8.5.13; 8.1 and older (EOL) also affected

title: OpenSSL EVP_EncodeBlock() integer overflow leads to heap buffer overflow (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)
why: OpenSSL published CVE-2026-121481 on Nov 18: calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length near INT_MAX overflows the output-size calculation and writes past the caller's buffer. The fix PR (openssl #33652) says the formal advisory is still pending; it reached Hacker News on Nov 20. Exploitation needs an application that base64-encodes ~2 GB of attacker-influenced data; no exploit or attacks reported, not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft signal.
action: Inventory OpenSSL 4.x builds and update to 4.0.4 or 4.1.1; watch for the pending OpenSSL advisory to confirm whether 3.x branches are affected.
product: OpenSSL 4.0 before 4.0.4 and 4.1 before 4.1.1 (3.x status unclear in sources)

title: Linux KVM (AMD nested virtualization) guest-to-host escape CVE-2026-99312 demonstrated on DigitalOcean droplets
why: On Nov 18, Terra Security published a write-up of a KVM bug in INIT emulation (stale MMU context while a nested guest runs). They used it on an ordinary DigitalOcean droplet to map about 127 GB of host RAM read-only from inside a guest. The fix went into stable 7.3.5, 6.18.64 and 6.12.118 on Nov 17. Terra says many clouds are out of reach because they don't enable nested virtualization on AMD. The write-up describes the technique, but I found no published exploit code, no exploitation reports, and no CISA KEV listing. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV. Nov 20: Terra published the write-up (127 GB of DigitalOcean host RAM read from a guest, plus a 32-byte host kernel write on a bare-metal test server); covered by THN and DigitalOcean. Fixed in stable 7.3.5, 6.18.64 and 6.12.118 (Nov 17); many distribution kernels not yet updated. Not in KEV.
action: KVM hosts on AMD that run untrusted guests should move to kernel 7.3.5, 6.18.64 or 6.12.118 or later (or the distro backport). Until then, load kvm_amd with nested=0.
product: Linux kernel KVM (x86, kvm_amd with nested virtualization) before 7.3.5 / 6.18.64 / 6.12.118

title: NoisyTCP: Linux kernel TCP pre-auth remote crash (CVE-2026-99288), present since 4.4, full details public after embargo
why: Hyunwoo Kim posted the full NoisyTCP write-up to oss-security on Nov 15 once the linux-distros embargo ended. A remote attacker with no login can panic any Linux host that has a TCP listener and spreads packets over 2+ RX queues or RPS (default on most cloud VMs). Kim has a private lab PoC (5 s to 2 min against KVM guests), but no exploit code is public and nobody has reported attacks. Debian and Oracle UEK have fixed kernels. As of Nov 15-16, Ubuntu and RHEL/Rocky/Alma had no fix yet. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft/MSRC (Azure Linux) entry in the collected data. Scored low because the impact is DoS only: Red Hat 7.5, no NVD score. Nov 16 update: BleepingComputer and others now cover it; Debian and Arch ship fixed kernels, Ubuntu and RHEL trackers still list it as unfixed/affected; researcher has still not published exploit code and no attacks are reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: Patch internet-facing Linux hosts to a kernel with commit 4e2b3ef19e0e (6.12.117/6.18.63/7.3.4 or your distro backport) and reboot. Until a distro fix ships, Ubuntu/RHEL hosts can set net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=0 in every netns, or use a single RX queue with RPS/RFS off. Weigh the SYN-flood trade-off first.
product: Linux kernel 4.4 through 6.12.116, 6.13-6.18.62, 6.19-7.3.3 (TCP established-socket lookup); EOL 7.2 gets no fix

title: 'Hello Again': fTPM lockout rollback via RPMC flaws lets attackers with physical access brute-force Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN
why: Academic paper (arXiv 2611.18126, CCS '26, Nov 13) demonstrates end-to-end on locked hardware: a 4-digit Hello PIN in 40 hours, BitLocker 6-digit TPM+PIN worst case 20 days, by rolling back fTPM anti-hammering state (Winbond RPMC HMAC key leak via glitching; AMD controller not verifying increments; some AMD boards with no rollback protection). Per the authors, no vendor committed to a root-cause fix; Microsoft only raised its recommended minimum Hello PIN to 6 digits. No CVE, no MSRC advisory. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since Nov 18, still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 19 17Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch (Senserva KEV tracker), so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 20 09Z: no CISA KEV additions since the Nov 18 batch, so still not in KEV.
action: For lost/stolen-device risk, enforce Windows Hello and BitLocker pre-boot PINs of at least 6 (preferably 8+) digits or alphanumeric PINs via policy.
product: Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN on x86 systems using firmware TPMs (AMD, Intel, Pluton) backed by SPI flash
